messages.body_plain:
Comment by al...@bedatadriven.com:

Score: Positive

General Comment:
Great work!
r359 adds more detail to the error that you're getting, it should help
pinpoint the problem. You can also add target/generated-sources/r-wrappers
to your build path and step through R$primitive$sample.java to see if
something is going terribly wrong in the matching of R-language args to the
java method.

Note that the internal sample primitive that you're implementing takes the
length of the vector (integer) as it's first argument, maybe the problem
lies there? The R-language wrapper the primitive thusly:

.Internal(sample(length(x), size, replace, prob))

For more information:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/detail?r=358

messages.subject: Comment on revision r377 in renjin
messages.subject_clean: Comment on revision r377 in renjin
messages.body_plain:
Comment by mhsatman:

General Comment:
Converting C source code is generally straightforward expect the case it
includes too many goto's. Another issue is to convert pointers but it is
easier. I want to write a small article in practical code solutions blog. I
want to explain converting C source to Java when
1) Code includes pointer, multi-dimensional arrays
2) Spaghetti code that consist of too many goto's.

In psigamma() function, for example, I handled the goto's using a private
static class and seperate void methods. A similar solution is applied in
the bratio() method in random.Utility class.

That was the hard part of converting C source. But the psigamma() function
seems extremely aesthetic except its hybrid nature.

mhsatman.

For more information:
http://code.google.com/p/renjin/source/detail?r=377
